provenance: Lane split authored by Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator. technique_name/tactic reconciled against intel/cti-pipeline.json. All 39 IDs verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — Office documents containing XLM/VBA macros and executables inside ZIP archives arriving by email are strongly detectable via mail-gateway content inspection, macro-bearing-attachment policy, and mark-of-the-web enforcement

medium — Office apps (EXCEL.EXE/WINWORD.EXE) spawning script hosts, or user launching an EXE from a temp/archive-extraction path, is detectable via process-lineage analytics, though it hinges on user interaction

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — wscript/cscript executing a VBS from %ProgramData% invoked by explorer.exe is detectable via process-lineage and script-host command-line telemetry, though VBS is a legitimate admin scripting language
high — PowerShell script-block logging / AMSI captures IEX of downloaded content, WMI recon one-liners, and the characteristic 60-100s sleep loop; high-fidelity if PS logging is enabled

high — scheduled-task creation (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational log) referencing a VBS/COM trigger or an unusual binary, and remote task creation across AD hosts, are strong, well-covered signals

detection_candidates.technique_name: Hijack Execution Flow: DLL Search Order Hijacking
detection_candidates.rationale: high — a signed/legitimate binary loading a same-named DLL from its own working/archive-extraction directory (rather than System32) is a strong sideloading signal via image-load (Sysmon EID 7) analytics
high — a script querying root\SecurityCenter2 AntiVirusProduct is an uncommon, high-fidelity discovery behavior detectable via PowerShell script-block logging and WMI activity monitoring
medium — HTTPS/TLS to non-standard high ports is detectable via egress port-usage baselining and TLS-certificate common-name inspection, though it can be tuned out as noise

medium — a non-Outlook process programmatically enumerating Outlook addresses/contacts and driving mail send is detectable via Office add-in/COM automation monitoring and outbound-mail anomaly analytics

high — internal mail carrying an EXE attachment sent programmatically from a user endpoint to many internal recipients is a strong, detectable anomaly via internal mail-flow and attachment-policy monitoring

high — executable file writes to remote admin shares (ADMIN$/C$) followed by remote scheduled-task creation across AD hosts is a high-fidelity lateral-spread signal via SMB and task-creation telemetry

medium — a process performing mass sequential file overwrites with random/zero bytes produces a detectable burst of file-modify I/O; detection value is early containment, since by wipe time impact is already occurring — prioritize the pre-wipe precursors (oref.org.il geofence check, Hebrew-locale check, dropped MicrosoftEdge.exe/csrs.exe, wallpaper change)

high — a process writing a new wallpaper image and modifying the desktop-wallpaper registry value/Control-Panel key, especially paired with a dropped media file, is a discrete high-fidelity signal (and, in this chain, a late-stage impact confirmation)

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — off-victim domain registration is not visible in host/network logs; hunt candidate via the health/finance/country domain-naming convention, Cloudflare fronting, and TLS-certificate common-name pivoting

low — abuse of a legitimate third-party mailbox defeats sender-reputation checks; hunt candidate via anomalous outbound volume/recipients from a trusted partner and DMARC/authentication anomalies on inbound partner mail
medium — Havoc has published default profiles, named-pipe patterns and sleep/beacon characteristics detectable via network signatures and in-memory scanning, though operators can customize them
low — attacker-side staging is not visible to the defender until delivery; hunt candidate via retro-hunt of archive/PDF downloads from newly-registered themed domains
low — capability development is off-victim; the shared XOR routine is a code-overlap attribution/hunting signal for sample triage rather than a host detection

low — brand/authority impersonation is a social-engineering behavior with little host telemetry; hunt candidate via lure-theme clustering and lookalike-domain/sender monitoring plus user-reported phishing

medium — embedded links to newly-registered/URL-shortener domains and credential-harvest pages are detectable via URL reputation, mail-link rewriting/detonation, and proxy category, though redirection and IP-gating reduce sandbox visibility
medium — detectable at the click via proxy/URL-detonation telemetry, but depends on user action and attacker IP-gating of the destination

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
hunting_candidates.rationale: medium — a sideloaded/lure-host process spawning cmd.exe to open a PDF is detectable via process-lineage, though cmd usage is ubiquitous
low — direct native-API use for in-memory payload assembly leaves little discrete host telemetry; hunt candidate via sample/behavioral analysis rather than log detection
medium — regsvr32 loading remote/scriptlet or unusual DLLs (squiblydoo-style) is detectable via command-line and network telemetry, but regsvr32 is a common LOLBIN with many benign uses

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Event Triggered Execution: Component Object Model Hijacking
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — HKCU CLSID\LocalServer32 writes pointing at a user-writable script path are stealthy and blend with benign registry activity; hunt candidate via registry-write monitoring on Classes\CLSID keys referencing .vbs/%ProgramData% paths

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — name-based masquerading defeats name allow-lists; hunt candidate via signer/hash validation, path anomalies (e.g. MicrosoftEdge.exe/csrs.exe outside expected locations), and original-filename metadata mismatch

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Command Obfuscation
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — obfuscation is designed to defeat static inspection; hunt candidate via entropy/AMSI-decoded content analysis and unusual-user-agent C2 responses rather than direct log detection

medium — archives arriving by email/download that expand to an EXE + same-named DLL sideload set are detectable via recursive archive inspection at the mail gateway, but nested/multi-file archives can slip past shallow scanning

medium — runtime decode routines are partly observable via AMSI/script-block content and file-write of freshly-decrypted executables, but the key-from-network-response design frustrates static/sandbox analysis
low — the evasion logic runs inside the document before any host artifact is created; hunt candidate via static XLM/macro inspection for GET.WORKSPACE anti-analysis patterns

hunting_candidates.technique_name: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — a language/locale query is trivially common and the geofence is benign-looking; hunt candidate only in correlation with the surrounding wiper drop chain and the oref.org.il connectivity check
medium — scripted WMI enumeration bursts and an early outbound HTTP POST of host inventory to an unfamiliar domain are detectable, though individual host-info queries are common
medium — the scripted admin/privilege check is visible in PowerShell script-block logs, but user-context queries are also routine
medium — scripted domain/Domain-Admins membership enumeration is detectable via PS logging and directory-query telemetry, though it overlaps with legitimate admin tooling

medium — the anomalous/rare hardcoded User-Agent strings, HTML-tag-embedded payloads, and consistent beacon+sleep pattern are detectable via web-proxy and JA3/TLS + user-agent analytics, though Cloudflare fronting hides true C2 IPs

medium — second-stage downloads from C2 (payloads embedded in HTML, executable pulls) are detectable via proxy content and file-write-then-execute correlation, though obfuscated-in-HTML delivery reduces clarity
medium — PowerShell using GDI/screen-capture APIs and writing image files to %AppData% is detectable via script-block logging and file-create telemetry, though screenshotting has benign analogues
medium — accumulation of script/text/image artifacts in %ProgramData% and %AppData% is detectable via file-path monitoring, though these are common, high-volume directories
medium — HTTP POST of screenshots/host data back to the beaconing C2 is detectable via outbound-volume anomalies and proxy content inspection, though it blends with the C2 traffic itself
